ceilings.source: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 Series Laptops spec page (AI TOPS 992, memory bandwidth 672 GB/s); BF16 ratio from NVIDIA RTX Blackwell GPU Architecture whitepaper v1.1 Appendix A-C tables
ceilings.notes: Laptop SKU. peak_gbps = 672 GB/s is NVIDIA's published figure (192-bit GDDR7). peak_tflops is DERIVED, not printed by NVIDIA: dense BF16 tensor with FP32 accumulate (what PyTorch bf16 matmul uses) = AI TOPS / 16, because NVIDIA's 'AI TOPS' is FP4 with 2:4 sparsity, and in every GeForce Blackwell table of the whitepaper (RTX 5090 3352 -> 209.5, RTX 5080 1801 -> 112.6, RTX 5070 Ti 1406 -> 87.9, RTX 5070 987.8 -> 61.7) BF16-FP32-acc dense = FP4-sparse / 16. 992 / 16 = 62.0 TFLOP/s. Cross-check from clocks: 184 tensor cores x 128 dense BF16 FLOP/clk/TC (= 61.7e12 / (192 TC x 2512 MHz) for the desktop RTX 5070) x 2220 MHz (top of NVIDIA's laptop boost range) = 52.3 TFLOP/s; NVIDIA's 992 AI TOPS implies ~2.63 GHz, above that range, so the 62.0 figure is the optimistic one. Laptop TGP and clocks are OEM-configured (this machine reported a 120 W cap) and GPU Boost can exceed the listed boost clock, so treat the spec roof as approximate; the measured roof is the one to compare against. No sparsity.

ceilings.method: bf16 square GEMM, best median over sizes [4096, 6144, 8192] (30 repeats each); D2D copy of 1024 MiB (read+write counted) median of 30
ceilings.note: peak = max(start, end) measurement; see start/end for drift
